title: SharePoint: Agent Chat web part embeds Microsoft 365 Copilot agents in pages
summary: Hold: the blocking control is described as stopping an agent everywhere, although Microsoft limits its effect for SharePoint-created agents to Copilot Chat. The API also excludes US Government deployments, and blocking is not the only documented tenant-wide agent control. The rollout dates and the notice's permissions and data-handling statements are accurately reported.

claims.quote: This is a new web part available for modern page editors in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the web part can be configured to use any Microsoft 365 Copilot agent.
claims.quote: The web part can be configured to use any M365 Copilot agent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost and impact
claims.claim: The licensing model is per-user, with Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users identified by the notice as affected users.
claims.quote: Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Users must have access to the configured agent to use it from the page.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent. ... Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The default is user-opt-in: authors choose to add the web part, without a documented web-part-specific admin enablement switch.
claims.quote: Searched: '"SharePoint" "Agent Chat" "disable"'; 'Set-SPOTenant DisabledWebPartIds Agent Chat web part'. Read MC1559633 (authors add it; no admin action required), Manage access to agents in SharePoint, and Set-SPOTenant search excerpts; no specific enablement switch found.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describing the Agent Chat web part turned up in searches.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part"'; 'SharePoint "Agent Chat" "web part" licensing identity disable tenant setting price'. Read Manage access to agents in SharePoint and search excerpts; results describe other agent surfaces, not this web part.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No price, meter or credit rate specific to the web part is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" "meter" price credit licensing'. Read Microsoft 365 Pay-as-you-go services pricing, License options for Microsoft Copilot, and Copilot Studio billing-licensing; general agent charges are documented, but no web-part-specific charge was found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which identity this web part uses when calling an agent.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" "identity" authentication permissions'. Read MC1559633, Manage access to agents in SharePoint, and identity search excerpts; none describes the web part's calling identity.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not describe any approval step added by the web part.
claims.quote: Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center path to block an agent is Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking decides whether an agent can be used at all in the organisation.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Replace the row's governs text, including its rendered table heading, with 'Whether an agent is blocked in Microsoft Copilot'. Add to its note: 'For agents created in SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry, blocking affects Microsoft Copilot Chat only.' The existing note about unconfirmed web-part effects can remain. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions.

claims.claim: The block operation uses a beta API and is not a production-supported final API.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API is presented without a cloud restriction alongside a briefing that covers US Government deployments.
claims.quote:
| Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
claims.fix: Add this exact qualification to controls[0].note and the rendered table note: 'The API is available in the Global service only; US Government L4, US Government L5 (DOD), and China operated by 21Vianet are not supported.' Keep the feature's roadmap cloud list unchanged. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-block.

claims.claim: Blocking an agent created in SharePoint or Foundry affects only its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Documentation does not specifically state whether blocking removes an embedded agent from the Agent Chat web part.
claims.quote: Searched: '"SharePoint" "Agent Chat" "disable"'; '"Agent Chat web part"'. Read agent-actions and Manage access to agents in SharePoint: they distinguish blocking effects by agent origin but do not describe removal from this web part.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Blocking is the only documented tenant-wide control that acts on an agent itself.
claims.quote: You can uninstall first-party or external agents across the whole organization or for specific users or groups ... When you delete an agent ... A soft-deleted agent is unavailable to its maker and end users
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence after the controls table with 'Blocking is an existing tenant-wide control for an agent; its effect depends on where the agent was created.' In Risk assessment, replace 'the Block row in the controls table is the one documented tenant-wide switch for an agent' with 'the controls table records the existing Block control'. Retain the following documented limitation for SharePoint- and Foundry-created agents. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: No setting named specifically for the Agent Chat web part was found on Microsoft Learn.
claims.quote: Searched: '"SharePoint" "Agent Chat" "disable"'; 'Set-SPOTenant DisabledWebPartIds Agent Chat web part'. Read Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant excerpts; no named web-part-specific setting found. MC1559633 states no admin switch.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists a DisabledWebPartIds parameter.
claims.quote: ### -DisabledWebPartIds ... Type: System.Guid[]
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/set-spotenant?view=sharepoint-ps to sources for the existing Set-SPOTenant parameter statement.

claims.claim: No documentation found connects DisabledWebPartIds to this web part or publishes its web part ID.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Set-SPOTenant DisabledWebPartIds Agent Chat web part'; '"SharePoint" "Agent Chat" "disable"'. Read Set-SPOTenant parameter excerpts and Manage access to agents in SharePoint; neither supplies this web part's ID or a mapping to DisabledWebPartIds.

claims.claim: The chosen agent's configuration governs its accessible knowledge sources.
claims.quote: The Agent Capabilities section displays the configured capabilities for the agent, defining the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whatever data the embedded agent reaches is governed by that agent's own configuration' with 'An agent's configured capabilities define the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/debugging-agents-copilot-studio to sources; do not attribute this general agent statement to MC1559633.

claims.claim: MC1559633 says the web part does not change the agent's configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" "data" "configuration"'. Read MC1559633 and Manage access to agents in SharePoint. The notice says data processing is unchanged, but does not state that agent configuration is unchanged.
claims.fix: Remove ', which this web part does not change according to the notice'. The existing What's changing statement that SharePoint does not change how agent data is processed can remain.

claims.claim: The chosen agent has its own configured actions.
claims.quote: Agent actions display the action ID and version number, configured functions for the action, along with their matching and selection status.
claims.fix: Replace 'Whatever actions the chosen agent can take are decided by that agent' with 'Review the chosen agent's configured actions.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/debugging-agents-copilot-studio to sources. Keep the separate, supported statement that the notice describes no added approval step.

claims.claim: Charges for the chosen agent depend on that agent's licensing rather than a published web-part-specific price.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.
claims.fix: Narrow 'Any charge for the chosen agent follows that agent's own licensing; check the agent's owner for its cost' to 'Check the chosen agent's licensing and billing conditions with its owner; Copilot Studio documents billing conditions for agents used in SharePoint.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing to sources.
